references.text: God's blessing to humanity to be fruitful and multiply, now fulfilled through the children of Israel
God's blessing to Noah and his sons to be fruitful and multiply
God's promise to Abraham to make him exceedingly numerous
God's promise to Abraham that his offspring would be as numerous as the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore
God's promise to Isaac that his offspring would be as numerous as the stars in the sky
God's promise to Jacob that his offspring would be like the dust of the earth
God's blessing to Jacob to be fruitful and multiply
God's promise to Jacob to make him into a great nation in Egypt
Israel settled in Goshen, acquired property there, were fruitful, and became very numerous
Confirmation that Israel became a great, mighty, and numerous people in Egypt
The psalm describes how the Lord made His people extremely fruitful and more powerful than their enemies
Stephen's speech refers to the people growing and becoming numerous in Egypt as the time for the fulfillment of the promise approached
Fulfillment of God's promise of numerous offspring; Exodus 1:7 marks the beginning of the process that culminates in 1 Kings 4:20.
Historical continuity: From population growth in Egypt (Exodus) to completed entry and possession (Joshua).
Typological parallel: Isaiah uses the image of population growth from Exodus as a metaphor for future restoration.
